name: An INPS pension of a Swiss citizen in Zurich, entered as taxed in Italy: Switzerland taxes it and credits the Italian tax
workings: Under Art. 18 of the Italy-Switzerland treaty an INPS pension of a Swiss resident is Switzerland's; Art. 19 would keep a public-service pension in Italy only for an Italian citizen, and this person is Swiss only. So Switzerland taxes it although the plan says taxedIn: source, with a warning, and credits the 500.00 Italy charged (which Italy would refund).
Income 30,000.00. Federal taxable 30,000 - 2,700 (insurance, without pension contributions) = 27,300; tax 0.77% x (27,300 - 15,200) = 93.1700.
Zurich taxable 30,000 - 4,350 = 25,650; simple tax 100 + 144 + 320 + 5% x 850 = 606.5000; cantonal 95% = 576.1750, communal (Zurich, 119%) = 721.7350; personal tax 24.
The pension is all the income, so the Swiss income tax on it is 93.1700 + 576.1750 + 721.7350 = 1,391.0800; the credit is the 500.00 paid, less than that.
